notes: Total 18 (hard bucket 18-30). The chain is: author the multi-choice log-probs task YAML (fixed 4-choice set, mandated prompt template embedding query/title, per-document doc_to_choice gold selector) -> register it through the installed, importable granite_eval harness package -> run the registered task over cd-nano (a tiny deterministic token->class scorer) over the fixture dataset and confirm accuracy lands in the required window -> persist both a classification result and an MTEB-style retrieval per-task result under the canonical /app/results/<task>/<run>.json layout -> fetch the live leaderboard table over HTTP at runtime and emit the org/model of the row with the highest mean as a single trimmed line. difficulty comes from the runnable multi-stage generalization (hidden_case_generalization=3: the same /app/run_eval.sh must re-run on five fresh classification datasets plus two retrieval datasets, each through subcommands) and from the amount of wiring across file formats and tooling (tool_breadth=3: YAML task spec, importable python harness package, JSON/JSONL fixtures, python http fetch of an HTML table). hidden_case_generalization=3 and dependent_stages=3 dominate; the accuracy/n/correct/skipped numbers and the leaderboard top-model id must be reproduced byte/1e-6 exactly when recomputed independently from the shipped cd-nano model.
